components.name: Signal Ribbon
components.description: The one authored hero illustration: a teal–lilac–violet silk ribbon crossing a ghost topology.

narrative.overview: The portfolio is a late-modern civic prospectus: one continuous document that explains a working network engineer with the clarity of a public-service report and the presence of a design annual. It is not a case file, a cyber dashboard, or a simulation of paper. The ground is a cool bone-white field, the argument is set in ink navy, and a single violet signal carries action, current position, and verified status. The page is structured like a prospectus, not a landing page. A sticky 72px header holds the identity and the section index; the hero pairs a two-line statement with one authored silk ribbon; the rest of the record is ruled into full-width bands for profile, capabilities, deployments, experience, credentials, and contact. Hairlines, index numerals, and monospaced metadata do the organizing. There are no lifted cards, paper textures, or decorative shadows. Dark mode is the same prospectus after hours: a deep-indigo ground with the same hierarchy, not a separate theme.
keyCharacteristics: One continuous ruled document with a sticky header and a left-aligned hero, never a centered landing-page shell.
A single violet signal for actions, current section, focus, and verified status; teal and lilac appear only inside the ribbon and route figure.
Albert Sans at 400/500 for display, reading, and headings; JetBrains Mono for file metadata, labels, and measurements.
Flat surfaces, 1px hairlines, 12px panels, 8px controls, and no casts or simulated material.
A complete FR/EN mirror, a pre-paint theme switch, and a dark mode that inverts the same tokens.
No invented evidence; the ribbon and favicon are SVG and the only shipping rasters are the processed logos.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Violet may occupy no more than roughly a tenth of any viewport. It belongs to action, current position, focus, and verification; if it starts coloring whole sections, the page has lost its hierarchy.

rules.name: The Unpainted Document Rule
rules.body: There is no paper fiber, grain, desk, folder, stamp, or cast shadow. Depth comes from ground-versus-sheet value and 1px rules. The page is a document, not a photograph of one.

rules.name: The Day/Night Prospectus Rule
rules.body: Dark mode is a full inversion of the same sheet, ink, hairline, and signal roles. It is not a tint, a neon skin, or a second brand.

rules.name: The Metadata Is Not Body Copy Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is for labels, measurements, and controls. It never sets a paragraph, because the page is technical without making the reader decode a terminal.

rules.name: The One Display Voice Rule
rules.body: Albert Sans carries both display and reading. Do not introduce a second display face to manufacture editorial contrast; scale, weight, and the violet line do that work.

rules.name: The Flat Prospectus Rule
rules.body: If an element needs a shadow to be understood, the hierarchy is wrong. Use a hairline, a surface change, or more space instead. A state change may use color and a 2px focus outline; it may not use a cast.

rules.name: The No-Costume Geometry Rule
rules.body: Do not add diagonal cuts, chamfers, blobs, or many-vertex clip paths. The document is orthogonal; the ribbon is the one curve.

dos: Do keep violet to action, current position, focus, and verification; sample the screen and keep it near or below 10%.
Do use 1px hairlines, ground-versus-sheet value, and space for hierarchy (12px panels, 8px controls, 1px rules).
Do set display and body in Albert Sans at 400/500; set labels and measurements in JetBrains Mono at 0.625–0.6875rem.
Do preserve the 1180px rail, the 72px/64px header, and the left-aligned 48/52 hero.
Do invert the same tokens for dark mode: Night Ground, Night Sheet, Night Ink, Night Violet.
Do keep every user-visible string paired FR/EN and every icon in the authored SVG sprite.
Do keep the contact action primary and the CV secondary until assets/cv.pdf exists.
donts: Don't add paper, grain, desk, folder, stamp, tape, or cast-shadow effects; this is a prospectus, not a case file.
Don't use gradient text, glass, blur, neon glows, or a second illustration system.
Don't turn bands into equal icon cards, nested cards, or a dashboard of tiles.
Don't use teal or lilac as UI accents; they belong to the ribbon and route figure.
Don't set paragraphs in mono, or introduce Alumni Sans, a condensed display face, or a system display face.
Don't invent certification badges, project screenshots, client logos, testimonials, or a CV.
Don't add a shadow to a panel or button; use a hairline, a surface change, or a state color.
